extracted.intended_audience: Prospective ONR applicants: researchers, industry, small businesses, and contractors seeking Navy/Marine Corps funding or contracts
extracted.subtask_description: Agency guidance describing ONR solicitation types, procedures, evaluation rules, and submission requirements for research, development, and acquisition proposals (including unsolicited proposals, CSOs, RFPs, RFQs, RFIs, SeaPort task orders, and sole-source J&As).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference to respond to open solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The preferred method for submitting ideas and concepts to ONR, in lieu of submission of an Unsolicited Proposal, is to respond to an open solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Types of solicitations used by ONR include: BAAs, SBIR topics, STTR topics, RFPs, NOFOs, or other ONR-sponsored solicitations. For more detailed information on how to find ONR solicitation opportunities, review the sections above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad Agency Announcements (BAA) and Notices of Funding Opportunities (NOFO)
rubrics_metrics.description: BAAs and NOFOs are used to announce research interests and solicit performers for ONR research areas; they advertise requirements for scientific study and experimentation directed toward advancing the state-of-the-art or increasing knowledge rather than focusing on a specific system or hardware solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOFOs only result in the award of an assistance instrument; BAAs may result in the award of both acquisition and assistance instruments. BAA Calls are often released to focus attention on a specific topic and funding availability. ONR announcements are posted at https://sam.gov/content/opportunities or www.grants.gov and listed on ONR's announcements section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial Solution Opening (CSO) — purpose and competitive process
rubrics_metrics.description: A CSO is a competitive process to acquire innovative commercial products and commercial services through competitive selection of proposals resulting from a general solicitation and the peer review of such proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A CSO may be used to obtain solutions or new capabilities that fulfill requirements, close capability gaps or provide potential technological advances, and may also be used to fulfill requirements for R&D solutions ranging from advanced component development through operational systems development. ONR announcements for CSOs are posted at https://sam.gov/content/opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: CSO definition of innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: For CSO purposes, innovation is defined as any technology, process or method, including research and development that is new as of the date of proposal submission or any application of a technology, process or method that is new as of proposal submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Proposal (RFP) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: RFPs are used in negotiated acquisitions to communicate Government requirements for supplies and services where there is a common statement of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ONR RFPs are posted at https://sam.gov/content/opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Quote (RFQ) criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: An RFQ is a solicitation that provides in exacting detail a list or description of all relevant parameters of the requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RFQs are best suited to commercial products and services. ONR RFQs are posted at https://sam.gov/content/opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Information (RFI) purpose and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An RFI is used when a government agency does not presently intend to award a contract, but wants to obtain price, delivery, other market information or capabilities for planning purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses to these notices are not offers and cannot be accepted by the government to form a binding contract. ONR RFIs are posted at https://sam.gov/content/opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Notice (SN) function
rubrics_metrics.description: An SN provides information about Industry Days, other events and other information that, while not captured in one of the other funding announcements, may be relevant to a given opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ONR SNs are posted at https://sam.gov/content/opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: SeaPort procurement platform and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR uses SeaPort to acquire support services; SeaPort is the Navy's electronic platform for acquiring support services in 22 functional areas including engineering, financial management and program management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SeaPort portal provides a standardized, efficient means of soliciting offers from large and small businesses and their approved team members. All task orders are competitively solicited, awarded and managed using the SeaPort platform. The Navy conducts rolling admissions to allow new industry partners with participation opportunities. Get information on SeaPort Login (navy.mil).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sole Source Requirements and Justification and Approvals (J&As)
rubrics_metrics.description: A J&A is a legal document required by Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) for contracting on a sole source basis (i.e. not providing for competition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: J&As set forth the facts for the determination that a sole source contract is appropriate. Sole source requirements and J&As are posted at https://sam.gov/content/opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsolicited Proposal definition
rubrics_metrics.description: An Unsolicited Proposal is a written application for a new or innovative idea submitted on the initiative of the offeror for the purpose of obtaining a contract with ONR, and is not in response to an RFP, BAA, SBIR/STTR topic, Program Research and Development Announcement, or any other Government-initiated solicitation or program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preferred method is to respond to an open solicitation. If submission of an Unsolicited Proposal is the most appropriate course of action, note that there are strict policies and procedures concerning submission, receipt, evaluation, and acceptance or rejection as set forth in FAR Subpart 15.6 – Unsolicited Proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required for an Unsolicited Proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance regarding the content that should be included in a properly submitted unsolicited proposal is provided in FAR Part 15.605.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visit FAR Part 15.605 for detailed guidance on required content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper marking for limited-use data in Unsolicited Proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: If the offeror wishes to restrict the data, the title page must be properly marked using the language referenced in FAR Part 15.609 – Limited Use of Data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unsolicited proposal may include data that the offeror does not want disclosed to the public for any purpose or used by the Government except for evaluation purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission point for Unsolicited Proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: All Unsolicited Proposals shall be submitted to the specified ONR email address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation procedures for Unsolicited Proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: All unsolicited proposals are reviewed in accordance with FAR Part 15.603 and evaluated in accordance with FAR Part(s) 15.606-1 and 15.606-2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the cited FAR parts for the review/evaluation criteria and procedures used by the Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility and Organizational Conflicts of Interest (OCI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements concerning responsible prospective contractors are governed by FAR Subpart 9.1, and policies addressing organizational conflicts of interest are governed by FAR Subpart 9.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To ensure fairness in consideration of proposals for ONR systems engineering and technical assistance and/or support services, ONR has implemented policies to protect against organizational conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where ONR posts funding opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR announcements are posted at https://sam.gov/content/opportunities or www.grants.gov; for convenience these opportunities are also listed on the announcements section of the ONR website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated throughout the page as the primary sources for locating active ONR solicitations including BAAs, CSOs, RFPs, RFQs, RFIs, SNs, J&As, and SeaPort opportunities.
